# support-coach

A LoRA adapter fine-tuned with Muse Muse on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B.

- Base: Qwen3.5-0.8B, https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B at revision 23c69c53358a07516b5827588b3fdb12ae78fd65
- Base builds on this drive: Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf
- Adapter: support-coach.gguf, from llama.cpp b11970 convert_lora_to_gguf.py, f32
- Dataset: support-coach, 49 examples
- Training: 60 steps, rank 8, learning rate 0.0002, examples up to 512 tokens
- Final loss 0.41, after 812 seconds, at most 1.91 GiB of GPU memory

## License

Qwen3.5-0.8B is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (licenses/Apache-2.0.txt). This fine-tune wasn't made,
reviewed or endorsed by its makers. What was changed is in licenses/CHANGES.md.

support-coach, on a Muse Muse flash drive

Open "Start Here.html" in your browser first. It works offline.

Everything on this drive runs on your computer. Nothing is downloaded, and nothing
you type leaves your computer.

It runs on a Mac with Apple silicon and 8 GB of memory or more, or a Windows PC with a 4 GB graphics card or 32 GB of memory.

  Mac with Apple silicon:  double-click "Start (Mac).command"
  Windows PC (x64):        double-click "Start (Windows).cmd"

Start picks the build that fits your computer, offers to copy it there, and opens
the chat in your browser. Close its window to stop the model. Windows PCs with
Smart App Control on aren't supported yet.

To check the files, double-click "Verify (Mac).command" or "Verify (Windows).cmd".
They compare every file with SHA256SUMS and change nothing. A drive that arrived
broken, or a file that doesn't match? To get a new one, ask whoever gave you this drive.

The drive doesn't run on Linux or on a Mac with an Intel chip. Muse Muse, which
made it, is at https://muse-muse.vercel.app

Fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-0.8B (Apache 2.0) on a Jetson. Not made, reviewed or
endorsed by its makers. What was changed is in licenses/CHANGES.md, and its
license is licenses/Apache-2.0.txt. The runtime is llama.cpp b0001 (0.0.1) (MIT).

#!/bin/bash
# Starts the model on this drive on a Mac with Apple silicon. Double-click it in Finder.
#
# It never downloads anything. It reads this Mac's memory, picks the build that fits (support/builds.tsv, the same
# table the Muse Muse website uses), offers to copy that build to this Mac, then starts the llama.cpp server from this
# drive on 127.0.0.1 only and opens its chat page in your browser. Close this window to stop the model.

set -u

DRIVE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SUPPORT="$DRIVE/support"
COPY_ROOT="$HOME/Muse Muse"

tell() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }

finish() {
  tell ""
  tell "$1"
  tell ""
  read -r -p "Press Return to close this window. " _ || true
  exit "${2:-1}"
}

ask_yes() {
  # $1: the question. $2: "y" or "n", the answer when the person just presses Return.
  local answer
  read -r -p "$1 " answer || answer=""
  [ -z "$answer" ] && answer="$2"
  case "$answer" in [Yy]*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}

value_of() {
  # The value of key $1 in support/model.tsv.
  local key value
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value; do
    if [ "$key" = "$1" ]; then printf '%s' "$value"; return 0; fi
  done < "$SUPPORT/model.tsv"
  return 1
}

sum_of() {
  # The sha256 SHA256SUMS lists for path $1, relative to the drive.
  local sum path
  while read -r sum path; do
    if [ "$path" = "$1" ]; then printf '%s' "$sum"; return 0; fi
  done < "$DRIVE/SHA256SUMS"
  return 1
}

[ -f "$SUPPORT/builds.tsv" ] && [ -f "$SUPPORT/files.tsv" ] && [ -f "$SUPPORT/model.tsv" ] ||
  finish "This drive is missing its support folder. Run Verify (Mac).command to check its files."

TITLE="$(value_of title)"
SLUG="$(value_of slug)"
[ -n "$SLUG" ] || SLUG="model"
PAGE="$(value_of page)"
[ -n "$PAGE" ] || PAGE="the model's page on the Muse Muse website"
# A model fine-tuned on a board is its base build with a LoRA adapter on top, as the board ran it (support/model.tsv).
ADAPTER="$(value_of adapter)"
if [ -n "$ADAPTER" ] && [ ! -f "$DRIVE/model/$ADAPTER" ]; then
  finish "The adapter $ADAPTER is missing from this drive. Run Verify (Mac).command to check its files."
fi
copy_adapter() {
  # It goes with the build. A copy that doesn't match its checksum is deleted, and the drive's own is used.
  cp "$DRIVE/model/$ADAPTER" "$COPY/model/" || return 0
  [ "$(shasum -a 256 "$COPY/model/$ADAPTER" | awk '{ print $1 }')" = "$(sum_of "model/$ADAPTER")" ] || rm -f "$COPY/model/$ADAPTER"
}
tell "$TITLE, from a Muse Muse flash drive."
tell ""

# 1. The machine. uname -m says x86_64 in a Rosetta Terminal, so ask the hardware itself.
if [ "$(sysctl -n hw.optional.arm64 2>/dev/null)" != "1" ]; then
  finish "This Mac has an Intel chip. The model on this drive needs a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later)."
fi
MEM_BYTES="$(sysctl -n hw.memsize 2>/dev/null)"
case "$MEM_BYTES" in '' | *[!0-9]*) MEM_BYTES=0 ;; esac
MEM_GB=$((MEM_BYTES / 1073741824))
CHIP="$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null)"
tell "This Mac: ${CHIP:-Apple silicon}, $MEM_GB GB of memory."

# 2. The build: the row for the largest memory size this Mac has at least.
BEST=-1 LEVEL="" FIT="" MIN_MAC=""
while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind mem vram level runtime fit where; do
  [ "$kind" = "mac" ] || continue
  if [ "$level" != "-" ] && [ -z "$MIN_MAC" ]; then MIN_MAC="$mem"; fi
  if [ "$mem" -le "$MEM_GB" ] && [ "$mem" -gt "$BEST" ]; then
    BEST="$mem" LEVEL="$level" FIT="$fit"
  fi
done < "$SUPPORT/builds.tsv"

SMALLEST=""
while IFS=$'\t' read -r level name bytes; do
  [ "$level" = "level" ] && continue
  [ -z "$SMALLEST" ] && SMALLEST="$level"
done < "$SUPPORT/files.tsv"

if [ -z "$LEVEL" ] || [ "$LEVEL" = "-" ]; then
  tell ""
  if [ -n "$MIN_MAC" ]; then
    tell "This model needs a Mac with $MIN_MAC GB of memory or more, and this one has $MEM_GB GB."
  else
    tell "None of the builds on this drive fits a Mac's memory."
  fi
  tell "It would run very slowly here, if at all, and other apps would slow down too."
  ask_yes "Try the smallest build anyway? [y/N]" n || finish "Nothing was started. Try it live instead, on its page: $PAGE" 0
  LEVEL="$SMALLEST" FIT="no"
fi

NAME="" BYTES=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r level name bytes; do
  if [ "$level" = "$LEVEL" ]; then NAME="$name" BYTES="$bytes"; fi
done < "$SUPPORT/files.tsv"
[ -n "$NAME" ] && [ -f "$DRIVE/model/$NAME" ] || finish "The $LEVEL build is missing from this drive. Run Verify (Mac).command to check its files."
# Rounded to the nearest GB, as Windows and the website show it.
SIZE_GB=$(((BYTES + 500000000) / 1000000000))

case "$FIT" in
  well) tell "The $LEVEL build ($SIZE_GB GB) runs well on this Mac." ;;
  tight) tell "The $LEVEL build ($SIZE_GB GB) runs on this Mac if you close other apps first, since it uses most of the memory." ;;
  *) tell "Starting the $LEVEL build ($SIZE_GB GB). Expect it to be slow." ;;
esac
tell ""

# 3. Copy it to this Mac, if the person agrees: loads are faster and the drive can come out.
RUN_DIR="$DRIVE"
WANT_SUM="$(sum_of "model/$NAME")"
COPY="$COPY_ROOT/$SLUG"
if [ -n "$WANT_SUM" ] && [ -f "$COPY/model/$NAME" ] && [ "$(cat "$COPY/model/$NAME.verified" 2>/dev/null)" = "$WANT_SUM" ]; then
  tell "Using the copy on this Mac, in $COPY."
  RUN_DIR="$COPY"
elif ask_yes "Copy the $LEVEL build to this Mac first? Loads are faster, and you can take the drive out. [Y/n]" y; then
  FREE_KB="$(df -k "$HOME" | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }')"
  case "$FREE_KB" in '' | *[!0-9]*) FREE_KB=0 ;; esac
  NEED_KB=$((BYTES / 1024 + 5 * 1024 * 1024))
  if [ "$FREE_KB" -lt "$NEED_KB" ]; then
    tell "There isn't room to copy it: it needs $((NEED_KB / 1024 / 1024)) GB free, and this Mac has $((FREE_KB / 1024 / 1024)) GB. Running it from the drive instead."
  else
    # At about 100 MB/s from a USB 3 drive; a slower drive or port takes longer.
    COPY_MIN=$((BYTES / 6000000000 + 1))
    tell "Copying $SIZE_GB GB to $COPY. This takes about $COPY_MIN minutes, and nothing shows here until it's done."
    rm -rf "$COPY/runtime" "$COPY/model"
    if mkdir -p "$COPY/model" "$COPY/runtime" &&
      cp -R "$DRIVE/runtime/macos-arm64" "$COPY/runtime/" &&
      chmod +x "$COPY/runtime/macos-arm64/llama-server" &&
      cp "$DRIVE/model/ui-config.json" "$DRIVE/model/system.txt" "$COPY/model/" &&
      { [ ! -f "$DRIVE/model/tuned.jinja" ] || cp "$DRIVE/model/tuned.jinja" "$COPY/model/"; } &&
      { [ -z "$ADAPTER" ] || copy_adapter; } &&
      cp "$DRIVE/model/$NAME" "$COPY/model/$NAME"; then
      tell "Checking the copy against its checksum."
      GOT_SUM="$(shasum -a 256 "$COPY/model/$NAME" | awk '{ print $1 }')"
      if [ -n "$WANT_SUM" ] && [ "$GOT_SUM" = "$WANT_SUM" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$WANT_SUM" > "$COPY/model/$NAME.verified"
        RUN_DIR="$COPY"
        tell "The copy matches. You can take the drive out once the chat opens."
      else
        rm -f "$COPY/model/$NAME"
        tell "The copy didn't match its checksum, so it was deleted. Running it from the drive instead."
      fi
    else
      rm -f "$COPY/model/$NAME"
      tell "The copy didn't finish. Running it from the drive instead."
    fi
  fi
fi

# 4. A free port on 127.0.0.1, then the server, with the chat's system message preset (model/ui-config.json).
PORT=""
for p in $(seq 9931 9950); do
  if ! nc -z 127.0.0.1 "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then PORT="$p"; break; fi
done
[ -n "$PORT" ] || finish "Ports 9931 to 9950 are all in use on this Mac. Quit the other model server and try again."

SERVER="$RUN_DIR/runtime/macos-arm64/llama-server"
ARGS=(-m "$RUN_DIR/model/$NAME" --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --offline --jinja -c 8192 --no-mmproj -np 1 --temp 0
  --ui-config-file "$RUN_DIR/model/ui-config.json")
if [ -f "$RUN_DIR/model/tuned.jinja" ]; then
  # A model trained before it learned to open its answer itself needs the template that opens it.
  ARGS+=(--chat-template-file "$RUN_DIR/model/tuned.jinja" --skip-chat-parsing --reasoning off)
fi
if [ -n "$ADAPTER" ]; then
  # The copy's adapter when the copy has one, else the drive's.
  LORA="$RUN_DIR/model/$ADAPTER"
  [ -f "$LORA" ] || LORA="$DRIVE/model/$ADAPTER"
  ARGS+=(--lora "$LORA")
fi

"$SERVER" "${ARGS[@]}" &
PID=$!
trap 'kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null' EXIT HUP INT TERM
tell ""
tell "Loading the model. The first time after copying or plugging in the drive can take up to 10 minutes."
tell "The server's messages scroll by below while it loads. That's normal: the chat opens once it's ready."

READY=""
for _ in $(seq 1 600); do
  kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || finish "The model server stopped before it was ready. Its messages are above."
  if curl -fs --max-time 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then READY=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
[ -n "$READY" ] || finish "The model didn't finish loading in 10 minutes. Close other apps and try again."

open "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/"
tell ""
tell "The chat is open at http://127.0.0.1:$PORT in your browser. Only this Mac can reach it."
tell "Keep this window open while you use it. Close it to stop the model."
wait "$PID"

@echo off
rem Starts the model on this drive on a Windows PC. Double-click it.
rem It never downloads anything: support\start-windows.ps1 reads this PC's memory and graphics card, picks the build
rem that fits, offers to copy it to this PC, then starts the llama.cpp server on 127.0.0.1 only and opens its chat page.
rem Close this window to stop the model.
setlocal
cd /d "%~dp0"
if /i "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" goto arm
if /i "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432%"=="ARM64" goto arm
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0support\start-windows.ps1"
echo.
pause
exit /b 0

:arm
echo This PC has an Arm processor. The model server on this drive is built for x64 PCs, so it can't run here yet.
echo.
pause
exit /b 1

support-coach

On a Muse Muse flash drive. Everything runs on your computer: nothing is downloaded, and nothing you type leaves it.

Will it run on your computer?

It runs on a Mac with Apple silicon and 8 GB of memory or more, or a Windows PC with a 4 GB graphics card or 32 GB of memory. Start picks the build that fits your computer and tells you why.

BuildSizeFor
Q4_K_M0.0 GBa Mac with 8 GB or more; a PC with a graphics card of 4 GB or more; a PC with 32 GB of memory and no big graphics card, slowly

Start it

On a Mac with Apple silicon

  1. Double-click Start (Mac).command on this drive. A Terminal window opens.
  2. If macOS says it can't be opened, open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway next to its name. Then double-click it again. This drive's launchers aren't signed yet.
  3. If macOS asks whether Terminal may open files on a removable volume, click Allow.
  4. Press Return to copy the model to your Mac (recommended), then wait. The chat opens in your browser.

On a Windows PC

  1. Double-click Start (Windows).cmd on this drive. A window opens.
  2. If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway. This drive's launchers aren't signed yet.
  3. Press Enter to copy the model to your PC (recommended), then wait. The chat opens in your browser.

Windows PCs with Smart App Control on aren't supported yet. To see whether yours has it on, open Windows Security, then App & browser control, then Smart App Control settings.

The first start can take up to 10 minutes while the model loads, and the window shows the server's messages as they scroll by. Keep the window open while you chat, and close it to stop the model.

The drive doesn't run on Linux or on a Mac with an Intel chip.

Chat with it

The chat opens at http://127.0.0.1:9931, or the next free port, and only your computer can reach it. Each new chat starts with the system message the model was trained with. If one doesn't, paste this into the chat's settings as its system message:

You are the support coach.

It is the base model with the adapter model/support-coach.gguf on top, as it ran on the board where it was tuned. The launchers load both.

Check the files

Double-click Verify (Mac).command or Verify (Windows).cmd. It checks every file on the drive against SHA256SUMS, and changes nothing.

About this drive

  • Fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-0.8B (Apache 2.0) on an NVIDIA Jetson, with Muse Muse. Not made, reviewed or endorsed by its makers. licenses/CHANGES.md says what was changed, and licenses/Apache-2.0.txt is its license.
  • The model card is MODEL_CARD.md, and PROVENANCE.json lists where every file came from.
  • The runtime is llama.cpp b0001 (0.0.1) (MIT), unchanged: licenses/llama.cpp-LICENSE.txt.
  • Made with Muse Muse: https://muse-muse.vercel.app.
  • A file that doesn't match its checksum? Ask whoever gave you this drive for a new one.
Drive image 2026.10.28-b11669.

#!/bin/bash
# Checks every file on this drive against SHA256SUMS. Double-click it in Finder. It reads the files and changes nothing.

cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
# Where to write about a drive that fails, as the drive's own support/model.tsv says it.
CONTACT="reply to the email your invoice came from"
if [ -f support/model.tsv ]; then
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value; do
    if [ "$key" = "contact" ] && [ -n "$value" ]; then CONTACT="$value"; fi
  done < support/model.tsv
fi
# How much there is to read: the sizes of the files SHA256SUMS lists.
BYTES=0
while read -r _sum path; do
  size="$(stat -f %z "$path" 2>/dev/null)"
  case "$size" in '' | *[!0-9]*) size=0 ;; esac
  BYTES=$((BYTES + size))
done < SHA256SUMS
GB=$(((BYTES + 500000000) / 1000000000))
# At 45 to 90 MB/s, as a USB drive reads.
echo "Checking every file on this drive against SHA256SUMS."
echo "Reading about $GB GB from a USB drive takes $((BYTES / 5400000000 + 1)) to $((BYTES / 2700000000 + 1)) minutes."
echo ""
if shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS; then
  echo ""
  echo "PASS: every file matches its checksum."
else
  echo ""
  echo "FAIL: the files marked FAILED above don't match. Copy nothing from this drive. For a new one, $CONTACT."
fi
echo ""
read -r -p "Press Return to close this window. " _ || true

@echo off
rem Checks every file on this drive against SHA256SUMS. Double-click it. It reads the files and changes nothing.
setlocal
cd /d "%~dp0"
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0support\verify-windows.ps1"
echo.
pause

# Changes

This drive holds a modified version of Qwen3.5-0.8B, which its makers license under the Apache License 2.0
(licenses/Apache-2.0.txt). As section 4(b) of that license asks, this is what was changed:

- Muse Muse fine-tuned a LoRA adapter on it on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (run support-coach: 60 steps, rank 8, from the dataset support-coach).
- llama.cpp b11970 convert_lora_to_gguf.py, f32 turned the adapter into model/support-coach.gguf.
- The base model's weights aren't changed. model/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf is a GGUF build of them, and the adapter loads on top.

The llama.cpp runtime (MIT, licenses/llama.cpp-LICENSE.txt) is release b0001 (0.0.1), unchanged. Only
the server and the libraries it loads are on the drive.

Qwen3.5-0.8B is its makers' model. This fine-tune wasn't made, reviewed or endorsed by them.
